solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wasted energy involves everyone as a rule

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or contain, so one piece wraps round the other
something wasted is ruined or wrecked, so the letters of energy are reworked

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A complaint that energy is usually squandered by everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' is the anagram signal and 'involves' wraps the rearranged letters round the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and 'as a rule' are synonymous adverbs meaning usually or in most cases.

clue.text: Looked to have organ around church

indicators.note: the organ is placed around the church, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a gland is a bodily organ
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone peered at an instrument set up to surround a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Beside 'church', 'organ' suggests the instrument; here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a quick look, so glanced is a past-tense synonym of looked.

clue.text: Marking zero — that's heartless!

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: A teacher grading with a nought, accused of cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter H from NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means observing or recording, as in marking something down or taking note of it.

clue.text: Apply to go up and down

definitions.text: Apply to go up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether going up or down the grid, a palindrome

parts.note: to consult a source or authority, turning to it for information or a decision

explanation.surface: An instruction to submit an application and then shuttle up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry the answer reads the same upwards and downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer can mean to consult or turn to a source or authority, as when one applies to it for information.

clue.text: Resin supplied by servant releasing key

indicators.note: letting go of something means those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a lackey is a servant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A resin provided by a servant who frees a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is a resinous secretion of the lac insect, used to make shellac.

clue.text: North-country folk irksome Henry upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Northern people annoyed a tiresome man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges IRKSOME HENRY. Yorkshire is a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Men of Yorkshire, a county in the north of England, are people of the north country.

clue.text: Something valuable quietly presented to lord

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
an earl is a lord

explanation.surface: A precious gift discreetly handed to a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem, and figuratively anything highly prized.

clue.text: Holy figureheads transformed into Spartans

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Religious leaders turned into warriors of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Patron saints are holy figures adopted as protectors and emblems of a place, trade or group.

clue.text: A bad person in charge holds me up at university?

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cad is an ill-behaved man

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in authority obstructs me at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the word, as this is a down entry, and 'holds' sets the result inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic describes scholarly matters of higher education, hence relating to life at university.

clue.text: Mechanic showing skill if joined by decorator

parts.note: art means skill
taken as written
an icer decorates cakes with icing

explanation.surface: A tradesman proves capable once partnered with a painter and decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorator' suggests a house painter, but it is someone who ices cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or a military mechanic, hence a synonym for mechanic.

clue.text: Couple who wrote American novels?

definitions.meaning: an old word for two, a pair
Mark ... wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn

explanation.surface: Wondering which pair co-wrote American fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is archaic for a pair, and Mark Twain is the pen name of the American novelist Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Shortens more than one agreement

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means makes or becomes shorter
... as a plural noun are formal agreements

explanation.surface: Someone trims down several deals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for shrinking and the plural of a noun for binding legal agreements.

clue.text: Conservative on mission for mastery

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a quest is a mission

explanation.surface: A Tory politician sent on a mission to gain dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Conquest is the subjugation of others, hence mastery or dominion over them.

clue.text: Numbers including crazy folk who can't settle?

indicators.note: to include is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A crowd containing some lunatics who can't calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' hints at calming down, but it means making a permanent home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wanderers with no fixed abode who never put down roots in one place.

clue.text: State of old character residing in British India

indicators.note: living inside means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: I is India in the radio alphabet
a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: The condition of a historic figure living in British India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition but is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a sovereign sultanate on the island of Borneo, so it is a country or state.

clue.text: Farmer, an Argentinian who fought between rivers

indicators.note: the pieces sit between the two letters for rivers, inside them

parts.note: R is short for river, so two rivers give two Rs
taken as written
Che Guevara was an Argentinian-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An Argentine agriculturalist who went to war between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a ranch, a large livestock farm, so is a kind of farmer.

clue.text: Very small interval — much less than an hour

definitions.text: interval — much less than an hour

explanation.surface: A tiny gap in time, far shorter than an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word spelt this way is both an adjective for tiny and the unit of sixty seconds.

clue.text: Joining a couple of hundred, accompanied by rebellious noises

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two give CC

indicators.note: rebellious means unruly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Signing up with two hundred others amid riotous shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Accession is the act of joining, as of a country to a treaty or an organisation.

clue.text: Sword penetrates a breast — just part of it

indicators.note: only a portion of the phrase is used, so the answer lies hidden inside these words

explanation.surface: A blade pierces someone's chest, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy cavalry sword with a curved blade.

clue.text: The best ointment?

definitions.meaning: the ... of something is its finest part
a soothing lotion for the skin

explanation.surface: Asking which salve is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the elite part of a group and a medicinal or cosmetic lotion.

clue.text: Cleaner to fix plant outside entrance to bathroom

indicators.note: fixing the plant outside the bathroom door means these pieces go around that letter

parts.note: to nail is to fix in place
a rush is a marsh plant

indicators.note: the entrance is the opening, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A cleaner is told to secure a plant beyond the bathroom door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person but is an object; 'outside' puts the two synonyms around the bathroom's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailbrush is a small brush for scrubbing fingernails, so a kind of cleaner.

clue.text: Where to drink during November

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Somewhere to have a drink in the month of November.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or tavern, a place serving alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Taken in and punished — not the first

indicators.note: leaving out the first letter of the word

parts.note: beaten means punished

explanation.surface: Someone duped and penalised, though not as the first victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like deceived, but means consumed as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten has been consumed, swallowed into the body.

clue.text: Boy, turning ten, always poetic as writer of verse

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A lad reaching ten is forever a budding poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like 'becoming' (a boy turning ten) but reverses TEN into NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer writes sonnets, fourteen-line poems, so is a kind of poet.
